thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike on /v1/streaming/generate (us-west2). Trigger: p99 > 1500ms for 5m, auto-pager escalated. Pager: @alex_oncall :rotating_light:

alex: Saw it, paging in. Initial dashboard: p50 120ms, p95 560ms, p99 2.1s, error rate flat. Appears concentrated on streaming route.

camille: Noticed correlated rise in batch sizes on the continuous-batcher consumer: median batch size up from 8 -> 32 on mixed-seqlen queues.

ben: Any customer-facing errors?

alex: No 5xxs, just latency. A few customers reported UI stalls. I DM'd support for customer list.

ops-bot: Support ticket link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-4987 (reported by support). Impact: 12 active sessions across 3 tenants with >1s stalls.

diana: Oncall + infra heads: paging pattern looks like long sequences (>=2048) are getting batch-packed with short sequences, KV cache miss churn spikes. Scheduler fairness appears to favor higher throttle queues, letting long ones wait and then floor them into large batches -> tail amplification.

eli: Can we temporarily cap batch size on streaming path to reduce tail? Patch idea: set CONTBATCH_MAX_BATCH=16 for streaming routers.

alex: Deploying a config change to constrain streaming batches and enable early-kick for long sequences. Rolling to us-west2 only first.

ben: What about preemptive sharding by sequence-length buckets? Might be faster but higher risk.

camille: Agree on staged mitigation: 1) cap batch size 2) enable seqlen-buckets in scheduler (experimental) 3) monitor p99 then decide on rollback.

alex: Pushing quick change now. Command: `kubectl set env deployment/contbatch-router CONTBATCH_MAX_BATCH=16 -n redwood-usw2`

ops-bot: Deploy started by alex at 1765512458. Rolling update to 6/6 pods.

incident-bot: NOTE: auto-rollout watch enabled. If latency doesn't improve in 5m, escalate to eng-runtime.

camille: Also flipping `EARLY_KICK_LONG_SEQ=true` on router; this causes long sequences to start their own batch after 100ms. Putting config in the same rollout.

ben: Any logs showing KV eviction churn?

alex: Logs: `contbatch: evict_kv_cache tenant=acme seqlen=4096 evicted=1 reason=pack_timeout` — seeing evictions within tail windows.

eli: Temporary tweak: reduce kv_cache_ttl for long seqs to avoid eviction storms. But that's risky for throughput. Prefer batching cap first.

ops-bot: Deploy completed at 1765512520. 6/6 pods updated.

camille: Early telemetry: p99 from 2.1s -> 1.0s within 40s of rollout. p95 down to 420ms. Looks promising.

alex: Noted one tenant still at ~1.2s p99, investigating logs for that tenant.

ben: Can you paste the non-prod repro config for the seqlen-bucketting? I want to run local sim.

camille: Config snippet (non-prod):
```
# seqlen-buckets config
SCHED_BUCKET_THRESHOLDS=[64,256,1024,4096]
SCHED_BUCKET_PREEMPT=true
SCHED_EARLY_KICK_MS=100
BUCKET_MAX_BATCH=[64,32,16,8]
```

camille: In sim this reduces mixed packing by 80% but increases small-seq latency a bit. We'll canary.

eli: For the tenant still hot: their traffic is 90% long sequences + intermittent spikes. I'm throttling their burst token bucket to smooth inflow while we stabilize. Applying `burst_limit=200rps` for tenant-id: acme-prod.

alex: Good. Applied tenant burst cap at 1765512605. Monitoring.

ops-bot: Support update queued (OPS-4987) — message: "We're mitigating a latency spike on streaming endpoints; we've applied temporary batching caps and tenant burst smoothing. We'll follow up in 30m."

camille: Telemetry 5m after patch: global p99 0.95s, acme-prod p99 1.05s. Error rate unchanged. KV eviction events dropped ~70%.

ben: Next steps? Do we want scheduler bucket canary to reduce tail further?

alex: I want to keep current caps for 30-60m, then canary seqlen-buckets on a single hostpool (us-west2-c) with extra logging. If good, roll more broadly.

eli: I'll create a canary job and a simple load pattern that mixes 90/10 long/short to validate.

camille: Also we should update runbook to include a step: "If p99 spike with mixed seqlen, apply CONTBATCH_MAX_BATCH=16 on streaming routers and early-kick long seqs."

ops-bot: Runbook patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runbooks/pull/312 opened by camille.

alex: Handoff: I'm going offline in 15m. @ben please take primary until next rotation. Keep caps in place unless p99 back to baseline.

ben: Taking over. I'll keep monitoring dashboards and liaise with runtime if canary shows any regression.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity lowered to S2. Customer impact reduced. Next update in 30m or on regression.

diana: Postmortem notes to capture: root cause likely scheduler packing policy + KV cache eviction interplay under mixed-seq workloads. Mitigations: short-term caps + early-kick + tenant burst smoothing. Long-term: seqlen-aware scheduling + smarter KV cache heuristics.

ben: A few action items assigned: eli - canary load job + tenant throttle plan, camille - seqlen-bucket canary PR, alex - monitor + confirm rollback criteria, diana - start postmortem doc.

alex: Thanks team. Marking thread as handoff to ben.

ben: Acknowledged. I'll post final resolution when we stabilize. :white_check_mark:
